Let <MATH_0001> be a site. Let
<MATH_0002> be a point of
the topos associated to <MATH_0003>.
The functor <MATH_0004>
has the following properties: It commutes with arbitrary limits,
it is left exact, it is faithful, it transforms surjections into surjections,
it commutes with coequalizers, it reflects injections, it reflects
surjections, and it reflects isomorphisms.

Because <MATH_0001> is a right adjoint it commutes with arbitrary limits and
it is left exact. The fact that <MATH_0002> is a canonically
split surjection implies that <MATH_0003> is faithful, reflects injections,
reflects surjections, and reflects isomorphisms. By
Lemma <REF_0001>
we may assume that <MATH_0004> comes from a point <MATH_0005>
of the underlying site <MATH_0006>. In this case the sheaf <MATH_0007> is given by
<MATH_0008>
see Equation (<REF_0002>) and
Definition <REF_0003>.
It follows immediately from this formula that <MATH_0009> transforms
surjections into surjections and coequalizers into coequalizers.
